LS11.P1.oracle: Independent literal fixture values and prohibited outcomes, not implementation roundtrip equivalence. Freshness threshold reached: literal expected source age10800seconds is stale while content/reschedule remain; counterexample must yield not stale at10799; independent reschedule survives stale transition. Offline startup without a cache: literal expected current time and four chosen metric fields work; no launch or fake timestamp; counterexample must yield generic geometry cannot fabricate a launch/countdown or make a nonexistent cache stale. Publisher stops but the file remains available: literal expected age continues increasing and stale appears; counterexample must yield fresh HTTP/build cannot clear stale or overwrite source-validation history. Previously tracked record is absent from a new provider result: literal expected A retains own older validation and pending status; counterexample must yield never copy batch freshness to A or infer A cancelled/launched from omission. Faster checking ends while data is stale: literal expected hourly cadence resumes but stale latch stays set; counterexample must yield do not clear latch until strictly newer validation for A arrives.

LS11.P1.statement:
The watch SHALL persist data and each record's provider-validation time. Freshness
MUST use source age, never download/build time. Default stale limits are three
hours normally and forty-five minutes near launch, configurable with publisher
cadence. Re-fetching old data or validating other records MUST NOT renew a record.
Once stale, that record SHALL remain stale until newer source validation arrives.
Cache SHALL survive restart; an empty cache SHALL show no schedule.
